# Fine-tuning and post-training

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/post-training.md) · ← [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md)

Supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation, reinforcement learning, parameter-efficient methods and distillation.

## Both tracks

- **Choose between prompt changes, retrieval and finetuning for a failing AI feature; include data freshness, latency and total cost.**
  - Applied scenario · Asked at: [Databricks](../companies/databricks.md) †, [Microsoft](../companies/microsoft.md) †, [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether the intervention matches the observed failure mode.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Classify missing knowledge, poor instructions and unwanted behaviour separately.
    - Establish a prompt baseline; test retrieval for fresh attributable knowledge.
    - Use finetuning when representative examples justify it, then compare lifecycle cost and held-out quality.
  - Read: [Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401) (Lewis et al., arXiv) · [LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) (Hu et al., arXiv)
- **Explain how Constitutional AI uses principles, self-revision and AI-generated preferences, and identify what human judgement it still depends on.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †
  - Tests: Whether reduced labelling effort is distinguished from removing human value choices.

## AI Engineering

- **Walk through a preference-based RLHF pipeline and explain the roles of the reward model and reference-policy penalty.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether data collection, reward fitting and policy optimisation are distinguished.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Separate demonstrations, preference pairs and policy rollouts.
    - Explain reward-model training and policy optimisation with a reference constraint.
    - Evaluate held-out human preferences and reward overoptimisation.
  - Read: [Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155) (Ouyang et al., arXiv)
- **Compare DPO with PPO-based RLHF, including the assumptions behind offline preference learning and reasons to collect fresh rollouts.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether a simpler objective is distinguished from universally better alignment.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Describe the preference objective using policy and reference log-probabilities.
    - Explain how it avoids a separately trained reward model in the basic formulation.
    - Discuss preference coverage and distribution shift rather than declaring online RL obsolete.
  - Read: [Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290) (Rafailov et al., arXiv)
- **Explain group-relative policy optimisation and the trade-offs of estimating advantages without a learned value model.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether relative rewards and variance are connected to sample groups.
- **Derive the low-rank weight update used by LoRA and propose an experiment for choosing its rank.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether parameter savings are linked to adaptation capacity and validation.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Represent the update as ΔW = BA and state both matrix shapes.
    - Compare trainable parameter counts with a full weight matrix.
    - Tune rank and target modules on held-out tasks; check regressions and merging constraints.
  - Read: [LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) (Hu et al., arXiv)
- **How does QLoRA reduce finetuning memory, and which tensors remain trainable or require higher precision?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether quantised base weights are separated from adapter optimisation.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Keep the base model quantised and frozen while training low-rank adapters.
    - Explain NF4, double quantisation and paged optimisers as separate memory mechanisms.
    - Account for dequantisation compute and remaining activation memory.
  - Read: [QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314) (Dettmers et al., arXiv)
- **Compare low-rank adapters, prefix tuning, soft prompt tuning and full finetuning for one task.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether data, capacity and deployment constraints guide adaptation.
- **After domain finetuning, general capabilities regress. How would you measure and reduce catastrophic forgetting?**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether task gains are checked against preserved capabilities.
- **Budget memory for full bf16 finetuning of a 7B model with Adam, then recalculate for LoRA and explain your optimiser assumptions.**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether gradients, optimiser state, master weights and activations are all considered.
- **When is a programmatically verifiable reward preferable to a learned reward model, and where can the verifier still be exploited?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether verification is treated as a specification with blind spots.
- **Policy reward keeps rising while humans prefer its outputs less. How would you diagnose and limit reward hacking?**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether optimisation of the proxy is distinguished from improvement in the real goal.
- **Design a teacher-to-student distillation process and explain how you would detect capabilities the smaller model fails to retain.**
  - System design
  - Tests: Whether data coverage and independent evaluation constrain teacher imitation.
- **A long pretraining run suddenly diverges. How do you investigate data, numerics and optimiser state before resuming from a checkpoint?**
  - Applied scenario · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) †
  - Tests: Whether recovery is based on a reproducible diagnosis.
- **Design training for a model that cannot fit on one accelerator; explain how you partition state and keep communication affordable.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) †
  - Tests: Whether model state, activations and network topology determine the parallel plan.
